market_commentary:
Canadian equities advanced as crude oil retreated in the week ending June 12 — the S&P/TSX Composite gained 1.52% to 34,937.9037 while WTI crude fell 11.74% to $80.58/bbl37, partially reversing recent supply-shock premium. The S&P 500 rose 0.65% to 7,431.46 and the Nasdaq added 0.70% to 25,888.8437. The Canadian dollar slipped 0.40% against the US dollar to 0.7148 CAD/USD37, with the Bank of Canada holding its overnight rate at 2.25% on June 101. The project database tracks 6,426 active Canadian capital projects valued at $1,536.5B in aggregate38.

Pipeline cross-references split along rate and commodity lines — all 6,426 active projects ($1,536.5B) finance against the Government of Canada yield curve anchored by the 2.25% policy rate, with the 5Y benchmark at 3.04% serving as the residential mortgage-renewal anchor for 257 residential projects ($36.2B)1. The 2s10s spread sits at 64 basis points after bull-flattening over the past year37. If WTI holds below the $74-76 breakeven band cited for Alberta oil-sands records, 89 active oil and gas projects ($63.2B) would face renewed margin pressure38, while copper at $6.5085/lb (+35.59% YoY) links to 532 active mining projects ($183.4B)37.
